correctness.rationale: The positivity, periodicity, monotonicity of f_j and of t f_j, and the product thresholds at zero and infinity meet Ishihara–Nakata's one-delay hypotheses. Thus the phase-indexed positive orbit exists, attracts, and is unique. In log coordinates, the unperturbed cyclic operator has symbol 2 cos(theta)-1 and a two-dimensional kernel E. Solving the complement and dividing the kernel equation by delta=1/lambda gives P(exp(-v_{j-1})-1-eta h_j)=0 at delta=0. For v_j=-q h_{j+1}, pairing opposite phases gives the stated hyperbolic-sine coefficient, and reflection kills its sine coefficient. The shift acts invertibly on E and the positive diagonal compression is positive definite, giving a nonsingular reduced equation even at q=0. The analytic branches agree for positive delta by uniqueness; a finite parameter cover gives the compact-eta error bound. Expansion and inversion give the two amplitude asymptotics. The finite-lambda susceptibility operator has symbol (2-delta)cos(theta)-1+i delta sin(theta), which has no zero among the six modes for 0<delta<1. Substitution of -(1-delta)h_{j+1} then gives the derivative with the reported sign and index.
